scope: Actual source callbacks executed with local storage and async mocks, no browser/cloud/credentials.

findings.trigger: Choose Corporate Credit Card in the simulated vendor-payment modal, empty card number/CVV/holder, expiry 99/99, then record.
findings.observed: The actual handler creates SUCCESS and the actual procurement handler accepts and saves the transaction.
findings.impact: The simulated payment marks a PO complete using invalid payment details; unlike the subscription label form, this form has no validation.
findings.limitation: Simulated payment only; no banking/payment provider was contacted.

findings.trigger: Type a full card number into the editable vendor-payment simulation form and record.
findings.observed: Synthetic test PAN 4111111111111111 is kept unchanged in local transaction accountReference and PO paymentInfo.reference/accountOrCard.
findings.impact: Full user-entered card numbers can be retained in localStorage and in the PO payment patch instead of a last-four-digit label.
findings.limitation: Synthetic input and local/mocked transition only. Actual Firebase write was not performed; the outbound patch is verified.

findings.trigger: Existing demo PO cache is a JSON array containing an invalid row such as [{}], then create a valid new PO.
findings.observed: Create reports success and writes the new valid PO together with the invalid row. Procurement then rejects the whole array as a corrupt cache.
findings.impact: A successful new PO cannot be opened through the order list until the old invalid row is recovered manually.
findings.limitation: Requires preexisting malformed cache. No normal form input producing the old invalid row was established.

findings.severity: P2 candidate with mocked session transition
findings.trigger: Start saving a receipt as A, switch to another staff account B while A getIdTokenResult is pending, then let A claims finish.
findings.observed: persistPoTransition calls authenticatedPost without rechecking captured A; authenticatedPost captures current B. The outbound receipt request is attributed to B.
findings.impact: A pending action from the previous account may execute under the next account when that account has receipt permission.
findings.limitation: Mocked auth timing; browser/Firebase account-switch lifecycle is not verified. Server still verifies B token and permissions, so this is not an authorization bypass.
